items.stem: For risk adjustment, a chronic condition can generally be captured when documentation shows it was:

options.text: Monitored, evaluated, assessed or treated during the encounter
options.rationale: Correct: MEAT criteria support capture of a chronic condition.

options.text: Mentioned once in the past medical history only
options.rationale: A historical mention without current MEAT support is insufficient.

options.text: Assumed because the patient is elderly
options.rationale: Age does not substitute for documentation.

options.text: Reported by a family member only
options.rationale: Provider documentation of current management is required.

items.explanation: Correct: MEAT criteria support capture of a chronic condition.

items.stem: Why might coding every documented diagnosis NOT always raise a patient's risk score?

options.text: Model hierarchies may override a lower category with a related higher one
options.rationale: Correct: HCC hierarchies prevent double-counting related conditions.

options.text: Only the first five codes ever count
options.rationale: There is no fixed five-code rule in these models.

options.text: Acute conditions always lower the score
options.rationale: Acute conditions are not a blanket score reducer.

items.stem: Which TWO practices support compliant risk-adjustment coding?

options.text: Coding only conditions supported by documentation
Confirming conditions are current, not resolved
options.rationale: Correct: resolved conditions should not be coded as active.

options.text: Adding codes to reach a target risk score
options.rationale: Coding to a target is non-compliant.
